docs.title: Upsight
docs.text:
End-user documentation for Upsight, the desktop app for technical CSMs at Kong.

Upsight keeps your account data, meeting notes, win wires, and external dashboards in one place. Everything is stored locally and works offline. Data syncs to and from Salesforce on demand.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
• Getting started, first launch, navigation, and basic setup
  • Install on macOS, download the .dmg, get past Gatekeeper, and install runtime dependencies
  • Install on NixOS, add the flake and install the package
  • Accounts, what accounts are and how to work with them
  • Account reference, People, Opportunities, Stack, Usage, Documents, Resources, and Events
  • Health and CX Events, posture indicators and logging customer experience events
  • Win Wires, generating a win wire from a PDF with AI
  • Agendas, building, enhancing, and presenting a meeting agenda
  • Q&A, AI-generated answers grounded in an account's data
  • Salesforce integration, authentication, sync, and write-back
  • Cases, Salesforce support cases across every account
  • Meeting summaries, AI summaries and the upsight summarize CLI
  • Monthly CX update, the guided wizard for refreshing an account's health picture
  • Action items, working Todoist tasks from inside Upsight
  • Feature Requests, Aha! ideas, ranking, and two-way comments
  • Dashboards, add and open external dashboard links
  • Backup and restore, automatic backups, manual backup, and restoring
  • Multi-machine sync, using Syncthing to share data across machines
  • Settings, a reference for every settings option

docs.title: Account reference
docs.text: Quick reference for the account tabs that are mostly straightforward data views rather than multi-step workflows, plus the global Events screen. See Accounts for the full tab list and Win Wires/Agendas/Q&A for the tabs with real AI-generation workflows.

docs.title: People
docs.text:
Three sub-tabs: Org Chart, People, and Teams.

People lists the account's contact directory (name, role, email, team, local time, and any tags). Use "Add contact" to pull a contact in from Salesforce (search by name or email, then import) or add one manually. Click a contact to edit it, set flags (Champion, Contact manager, Portal user, Academy user, Security contact, Primary, Executive), assign it to a team, or delete it. "Refresh from SF" re-pulls every Salesforce-linked contact; a per-contact refresh icon updates just one. If a support case names a contact that isn't in the directory yet, it appears at the top of the list as a one-click "Add" suggestion.

Teams lists the account's internal team structure (name, identifier, org). Expand a team to see its members. "New team" creates one; the edit icon renames it or moves it under a different parent. "Add collaboration" links two teams with a note describing what they work on together.

Org Chart renders the reporting hierarchy built from your teams, contacts, and collaborations. It stays empty until you've added at least one team.

docs.title: Opportunities
docs.text:
Salesforce opportunities for the account, open and recently closed. The header shows total ACV and open count; a risk-weighted pipeline bar breaks pipeline ACV into Green/Yellow/Red by renewal risk when that data is synced.

Expand an opportunity for its full detail: ACV/TCV, Sales Play, competitors, GEP field-completion percentage, Champion and Economic Buyer, the full MEDDPICC write-up (Identified Pain, Value Drivers, Metrics, Outcomes, Challenges, Decision Criteria, Decision Process, Paper Process, Requirements), the GEP checklist (Met Champion, VOC, Budget, PBOs Agreed), key dates (TFW, TVE, EB Meeting) with a MAP link, contract dates, and ARR churn forecast. Any linked Professional Services engagements show their remaining and total hours.

Everything here is read-only Salesforce data except two notes fields, CX Notes and CS Handoff Notes. Click "Edit" next to either to write a note; it saves locally and queues for write-back like any other field edit.

docs.title: Stack
docs.text:
The customer's technical footprint, entered and maintained by hand (nothing here syncs from Salesforce): Konnect orgs, products and plugins, and infrastructure, each grouped by category with an "Add" button. Click an entry to edit or delete it.

Map a Konnect org to one of your internal teams using the "+ team" picker under that org, so ownership is visible without leaving the tab. Click a mapped team's chip to unmap it.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: A read-only view of product adoption pulled from the account's synced Salesforce entitlement data: usage bars (used against contracted, colored red under 50%, yellow under 80%, green at 80%+) and value fields for Konnect, Cloud Gateway, Enterprise, Mesh, Insomnia, and production-date milestones. Nothing here is editable. It stays empty until entitlement data has been synced for the account.

docs.title: Documents
docs.text:
Attaches file metadata to the account, which also feeds the account's AI context (meeting summaries, Q&A, and similar draw on document descriptions).

  • Import file opens the native file picker, copies the file into Upsight's managed store, and records it.
  • Add by path records a reference to a file or URL without copying anything, useful for something that already lives elsewhere. Fill in the file name (the type is inferred from its extension unless you set one), the path or URL, and an optional description.

Click a document's open icon to launch it in your OS's default app for that file type. Edit the description inline, or delete the record (this removes only the metadata, not the underlying file).

docs.title: Resources
docs.text: A read-only, categorized set of links for the account: Quick Links, Channels (tagged Internal or External), and Konnect Orgs (which mirror what you've added under Stack and link straight to the Konnect cloud console). Click any link to open it in your default browser. Click a category header to collapse or expand it.

docs.title: Events (global)
docs.text:
Events is a global screen, not scoped to one account, listing system-driven activity across every account: Aha idea ships and status changes, and Salesforce field write-backs. Filter by system (Aha, Salesforce, Todoist) or category, or show unseen only. "Mark all read" clears the unseen badge.

Two actions are available inline, when applicable:

  • A shipped Aha idea can be converted straight into a Todoist task with the "→ Todoist" button, if Todoist write-back is enabled in Settings.
  • A field write-back can be reverted with the "Revert" button, which previews the change (old value, new value, and whether the live Salesforce value has since drifted from what was written) before you confirm.

docs.title: Accounts
docs.text: Each account in Upsight corresponds to a customer organization from Salesforce. Accounts are the primary unit of work. Most of the app's screens live inside an account context.

docs.title: The accounts list
docs.text:
The Home screen shows every account you have synced from Salesforce. Click any row to open that account. The search bar at the top filters by name.

Each row shows the account name and a summary of health indicators from the most recent Salesforce sync.

docs.title: Sections within an account
docs.text:
Once you open an account, the sidebar expands with these tabs:

  • Overview shows the at-a-glance summary: consumption gauge, health posture, recent activity, and upcoming meetings.
  • Health shows posture indicators and enrichment status from Salesforce, with inline editing. Field edits save locally and queue for write-back if Salesforce write-back is enabled (see Health and CX Events).
  • People lists contacts, teams, and the org chart for the account, pulled from Salesforce and maintained by hand (see Account reference).
  • Action Items tracks open tasks for this account (see Action items).
  • Meetings shows past and upcoming meeting records, with AI-generated summaries where available (see Meeting summaries).
  • Agendas holds meeting agenda drafts you can enhance with AI, export, or present (see Agendas).
  • CX Events shows customer experience events from Salesforce (see Health and CX Events).
  • Opportunities lists open and recently closed Salesforce opportunities (see Account reference).
  • Win Wires holds win wire documents. New entries are pulled from Salesforce and PDFs can be attached and AI-extracted (see Win Wires).
  • Stack shows the customer's technical stack: Konnect orgs, installed products and plugins, and infrastructure details. You maintain these manually (see Account reference).
  • Usage displays product utilization from account entitlements data (see Account reference).
  • Q&A stores AI-generated answers to questions you ask about the account (see Q&A).
  • Documents attaches arbitrary files to the account (PDFs, notes, and similar; see Account reference).
  • Resources holds links and references specific to the account (see Account reference).

docs.title: Syncing an account
docs.text:
Upsight pulls Salesforce data on demand, not on a continuous schedule. Click the sync button in the account header (the rotating-arrows icon above the tab strip) to pull the latest data. The app reads from your Salesforce CLI session (sf) and updates the local database.

Edits you make in the app (posture fields, notes, health indicators) save locally immediately. If Salesforce write-back is enabled, the app pushes those changes back to Salesforce in the background. See Salesforce integration for details.

docs.title: Action items
docs.text: Action items in Upsight are Todoist tasks. Upsight does not have its own task store, it reads, syncs, and triages tasks from your connected Todoist account. Set up the Todoist API token in Settings before either view below shows data. See Settings.

docs.title: Two views
docs.text:
Action Items (top-level sidebar, global) shows "Focused tasks", every task due today, overdue, or priority P1 through P3, across every account or scoped to whichever account you have selected in the sidebar switcher. Tasks are grouped by account. This view is read-only: it shows what needs attention and lets you sync, nothing else.

Action Items (the tab inside an account) shows only that account's tasks, with the full set of filters and actions.

docs.title: Filtering, inside an account
docs.text: Filter chips at the top switch between Focused, All, Overdue, Today, and Upcoming, each with a live count. If the account's Todoist project has sections, a section dropdown narrows further. Priority buttons (P1 through P4) filter by priority and can be combined. Check "Show completed" to bring finished tasks back into view.

docs.title: Working a task
docs.text:
Click the circle to the left of a task to mark it complete or reopen it. Hover a task to reveal defer buttons, snooze it 1, 2, or 4 weeks, or clear an existing defer. Click the chevron on the right to expand a task's Todoist comments.

None of this happens instantly against Todoist. Click "Sync" (per account) or "Sync all" (global view) to pull the latest tasks, completions, and comments from Todoist into Upsight.

docs.title: Where tasks come from
docs.text: Upsight does not let you create a task directly from either Action Items view. Tasks come from Todoist itself, or from the one built-in shortcut: when an Aha idea you're tracking reaches a shipped status in the Events feed, Upsight can offer a "create Todoist task" button there, if you've enabled "Todoist ship events" in Settings.

docs.title: Suggested tasks
docs.text: If "Todoist suggested tasks" is enabled in Settings, Upsight periodically flags tasks tied to your accounts that have gone stale (no activity for the configured number of days) and surfaces them as a Suggested group in the per-account view.

docs.title: Agendas
docs.text: The Agendas tab, inside an account, holds meeting agenda drafts. Write one, enhance it with AI, export it, or open it as a presentation.

docs.title: Creating and writing an agenda
docs.text: Click Add to create a new agenda, or select an existing one from the list. While you write, three reference cards show open action items (from Todoist, with priority badges), recent meetings, and open opportunities, so you have that context without leaving the screen. Click Edit to change the agenda's raw content directly.

docs.title: AI enhancement
docs.text: Enhance runs the whole agenda through AI to tighten and improve the writing. To enhance only part of it, highlight a passage in the compiled body and click Enhance selected, which sends just that passage and splices the result back in place.

docs.title: Adding release slides from Slack
docs.text: Updates (labeled "Select updates" in the empty state) opens a picker over product updates already pulled from your configured #releases Slack channel for this account, and splices the ones you pick in as release slides. This content is copied verbatim, not rewritten by AI, so the release facts stay exact. If nothing shows up, no updates have been synced from Slack yet for this account.

docs.title: Copying, exporting, and presenting
docs.text:
• Copy puts the compiled agenda markdown on your system clipboard.
  • Export saves the agenda's slide markdown to a file you choose, via the native save dialog.
  • Open Presentation builds a reveal.js slide deck in Kong's brand theme and opens it in your default browser, ready to present. This is a different output from Export: Export gives you the raw markdown, Open Presentation gives you the rendered deck.

docs.title: Backup and restore
docs.text: Upsight maintains automatic rolling backups of your database. Each backup is a single archive containing the SQLite database and your account files (documents, win wires, logos).

docs.title: Automatic backups
docs.text:
By default the app takes a backup every 24 hours and keeps:

  • 7 daily snapshots
  • 4 weekly snapshots

When the retention limits are reached, older snapshots are removed automatically.

You can adjust the schedule and retention in Settings under Data, "Automatic backups." Changes take effect on the next app launch.

To see when the last backup ran, go to Settings, then About. The Diagnostics panel shows the backup directory path and the timestamp of the last backup.

docs.title: Manual backup
docs.text: To take a backup immediately, go to Settings, then Data, and click "Back up now." Or go to Settings, About, Diagnostics, and click "Back up now." The app reports the filename when the backup completes.

docs.title: Backup file location
docs.text: Upsight stores backups in a subdirectory of its data directory. The exact path is shown in Settings under About, Diagnostics, Backups.

docs.title: Restoring from a backup
docs.text:
To restore, close the app and replace the database file with the backup copy.

The database file path is shown in Settings under About, Diagnostics, Database. It is also printed in Settings under Data, Database, "Path."

Steps to restore:

  1. Close Upsight.
  2. Find the backup file you want to restore from (in the backups directory shown in Settings).
  3. Copy the backup file over the current database file, overwriting it.
  4. Reopen Upsight.

Backup filenames include a timestamp so you can identify which snapshot to use.

If you have Syncthing running, pause the sync before restoring so Syncthing does not conflict with the file operation. Resume sync after the app starts and confirms the database opens cleanly.

docs.title: Compacting the database
docs.text: The "Compact (VACUUM)" button in Settings under Data runs SQLite's VACUUM command on the database. This rewrites the file to recover space from deleted rows and fragmentation. It is safe to run anytime, but it takes a few seconds for large databases. It also requires exclusive access, so the app must be the only process with the file open.

docs.title: Import and export
docs.text:
You can move account data between Upsight instances using the import and export tools in Settings under Data, "Import / Export."

Exporting produces a ZIP bundle with the selected accounts' full dataset, including contacts, opportunities, interactions, win wires, cases, tasks, meeting history, and attachments.

Importing reads a bundle and merges it into the current database. If the bundle contains accounts that already exist (matched by Salesforce ID), the import asks whether to skip those accounts or update them.

docs.title: Cases
docs.text: The Cases screen (Ctrl+2) lists Salesforce cases across every account, not just the one you have open. It is one of the global screens in the sidebar's top section.

docs.title: Syncing and filtering
docs.text:
Click Sync to pull the latest cases from Salesforce into the local database. By default the list shows open cases only. Click the account switcher in the sidebar first if you want to scope the list to a single account, use the search box to match a case number or subject, or use the priority dropdown to narrow by priority.

Click Closed to switch to closed cases. Closed cases are limited to the last 30 days, an indicator next to the count reminds you of that when the toggle is on. Older closed cases still exist in Salesforce, they are just not synced locally.

The status and priority bars at the top of the screen give you a quick read on how open cases in the current scope break down.

docs.title: Escalation and staleness indicators
docs.text:
Each row can carry two small icons next to the status and priority badges:

  • A red activity icon means the case is escalated, either its status is one of the escalation states (escalated to engineering, escalated to services, internal escalation) or it has a linked Jira ticket. A closed case never shows this, even if it was escalated before it closed.
  • A yellow clock icon means the case is stale, no comment (or, if it has never had one, no activity since it was created) in over 7 calendar days. A closed case never shows this either.

Open a case to see the same information as labeled badges in the detail panel header, along with Jira and Slack buttons when the case has a linked ticket or thread. Hovering a button shows the destination's domain before you click it, worth checking since these fields come straight from Salesforce and nothing stops them from being edited to point somewhere unexpected.

docs.title: Case detail and comments
docs.text:
Click a row to open the case detail panel. It shows the full comment and history timeline, and lets you post a new comment from the box at the bottom (Cmd/Ctrl+Enter submits). A posted comment saves locally and appears in the timeline immediately, it reaches Salesforce only if write-back is turned on, the same queue every other Upsight edit uses. See Salesforce integration for how write-back works.

Use the arrows in the panel (or j/k) to step to the next or previous case in your current filtered list without closing the panel.

docs.title: Dashboards
docs.text:
The Dashboards screen is a global shortcut list for external URLs you check regularly: Looker reports, Grafana boards, Salesforce list views, and anything else with a URL. Adding a link here means you can reach it in one click without hunting through browser bookmarks.

Dashboards are not account-scoped. The list applies across all accounts.

docs.title: Adding a dashboard
docs.text:
Click "Add Dashboard" at the top right of the Dashboards screen. Enter a name and a URL. You can optionally add an icon to make the entry easy to spot in the list.

Save the entry. It appears in the list immediately and stays there across app restarts.

docs.title: Opening a dashboard
docs.text: Click any entry in the list to open it in your default browser (the app uses your system's default URL opener).

docs.title: Editing and removing entries
docs.text: Each entry has an edit button on the right side of its row. Click it to change the name, URL, or icon, or to remove the entry.

docs.title: Reordering
docs.text: Use the up and down arrows on each row to reorder the list. The order is saved automatically.

docs.title: Jumping to a dashboard by name
docs.text: Use Ctrl+K to open the command palette. Type any part of a dashboard name to find and open it directly, without navigating to the Dashboards screen first.

docs.title: Feature Requests
docs.text: The Feature Requests screen aggregates Aha! ideas across every account you have synced. It is a global screen, not scoped to one account, reachable from the sidebar or Ctrl+4.

docs.title: Syncing from Aha!
docs.text:
Click Sync Aha in the top right to pull the latest ideas for every account. Each idea in Aha! is matched to the accounts that endorse it, and one row is shown per idea with a vote from each endorsing account. A sync that returns no ideas leaves the list unchanged rather than clearing it, so a temporary Aha! outage or a missing token does not blank the screen.

Aha! must be configured under Settings, Integrations, before a sync can pull real data. See Settings.

docs.title: Metrics and filters
docs.text:
The four cards at the top summarize the current account scope:

  • Total Ideas, everything in scope.
  • Accounts Linked, how many accounts endorse at least one idea (always counts across all accounts, not just the current scope).
  • Needle Movers, live ideas ranked in the top 3 by at least one account.
  • Multi-Customer, live ideas endorsed by 2 or more accounts.

Filter the list with the search box, the account dropdown (scope to one account or "All accounts"), the rank filter (Needle Movers or Top 10), the minimum shared-customer count, and the product chips (click a product label on a row to add it as a filter). Toggle Shipped to switch between live ideas and ideas Aha! marks shipped.

docs.title: The idea detail panel
docs.text:
Click a row to open its detail panel.

Rank. Each endorsing account gets its own rank on the idea, 1 through 10, or Unranked. Change it from the dropdown next to that account, this writes back to Aha! immediately.

Tracking details. Below the rank, each account has its own tracking fields: Requester (a contact from that account), a production-blocker flag, target release, use case, a source link, an internal discussion link, and notes. These save locally per account and idea, independent of rank.

AI-suggested use case. The "Suggest" button next to the use case field generates a draft from context Upsight already has cached for the idea. If the source link is a Slack URL, it instead reads that Slack thread, which needs Slack configured under Settings first. This can take a while, only one suggestion runs per idea at a time.

Comments. The comment thread is real, two-way Aha! commenting: posting a comment here writes it to Aha!, and it becomes visible to anyone with access to the idea there. Posting requires Aha! write-back to be enabled in Settings, Integrations. With it off, posting fails with a message telling you where to turn it on.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: Upsight is a desktop app for technical CSMs at Kong. It keeps your account data, meeting notes, win wires, and external dashboards in one place, all local and offline-capable, synced to Salesforce on demand.

docs.title: First launch
docs.text:
The very first time you open the app, it asks for a license key before showing anything else. This is a one-time step — once the key is accepted you won't be asked again on that machine, and if you use Upsight on more than one Mac or Linux box with the same synced config, activating on one covers the rest (see Multi-machine sync).

If you don't have a key yet, ask whoever administers Upsight for your team to issue you one, then paste it into the activation screen and click Activate.

Once past activation, the app opens to the accounts list (Home). On first launch this list is empty. Accounts are pulled from Salesforce the first time you authenticate and run a sync.

Before syncing, you need:

  • The Salesforce CLI (sf) installed and authenticated: sf org login web. The app uses your existing CLI session and never handles your Salesforce credentials directly.
  • An AI binary for AI features: the claude CLI on PATH and logged in. You can skip this and add it later under Settings.

docs.title: Navigating the app
docs.text:
The left sidebar has two levels.

The top section (Home, Action Items, Cases, Feature Requests, Dashboards, Events) is global. These show data across all accounts.

When you select an account from the Home list, the sidebar adds an account-scoped section below the global items. This contains tabs for that account: Overview, Health, People, Action Items, Meetings, Agendas, CX Events, Opportunities, Win Wires, Stack, Usage, Q&A, Documents, and Resources.

Click a different account in the Home list to switch. The account-scoped section updates to reflect the new selection.

docs.title: Keyboard shortcuts
docs.text: Shortcut Action Ctrl+1 Home (accounts list) Ctrl+2 Cases Ctrl+3 Settings Ctrl+4 Feature Requests Ctrl+5 Dashboards Ctrl+K Command palette (jump anywhere by name)

docs.title: Density and theme
docs.text: You can switch between light and dark themes (or follow your system setting) and between comfortable and compact row density in Settings under General.

docs.title: Where data lives
docs.text:
Everything is stored in a single SQLite file on your machine. The installed app (Nix-packaged on Linux, or the macOS .dmg release) uses ~/.local/share/upsight/upsight.db by default. Set UPSIGHT_DB before launching to point at a different file. The database isn't encrypted at rest, so consider full-disk encryption on your machine, or point UPSIGHT_DB at an encrypted volume.

See Backup and restore and Multi-machine sync for how to protect and share that file.

docs.title: Health and CX Events
docs.text: Two related, account-scoped tabs: Health, the account's posture indicators, and CX Events, a log of customer experience activity synced from and logged to Salesforce.

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
The Health tab shows ten posture indicators (Consumption, Enterprise Features, Kong OSS Present, Critical Use Cases, Customer Business Health, Relationship Health, Technical Engagement, Platform Play, Value Realization, Active Project), each with a status pill (Green, Yellow, Red, or Unset) and a notes field, enriched from Salesforce.

Click an indicator to open its editor and change the status or notes by hand. Saving queues a local write-back; nothing reaches Salesforce unless Salesforce write-back is enabled (see Salesforce integration).

For AI-generated suggestions across all ten indicators at once, rather than editing one at a time, use the Monthly CX Update wizard's Generate all (or generate a single indicator from its own row). See Monthly CX update.

docs.title: CX Events
docs.text: The CX Events tab lists customer experience events for the account. Click Log CX Event to record one, filling in a subject and the other event fields, this writes a new event to Salesforce. An event you log yourself can be deleted from Upsight; events synced in from Salesforce cannot be edited or deleted here; change those in Salesforce directly.

docs.title: Install on macOS
docs.text: Upsight publishes a macOS .dmg on every GitHub release. This is the path for anyone who is not building the app from source with Nix. See Install on NixOS if you are on NixOS instead.

docs.title: Download and install
docs.text:
1. Download Upsight.dmg from the latest release.
  2. Open it and drag Upsight into Applications.
  3. Launch it from Launchpad or Spotlight.

docs.title: Getting past Gatekeeper
docs.text:
The build is unsigned. There is no Apple Developer ID certificate behind it, so macOS Gatekeeper blocks a plain double-click on first launch with an "Upsight can't be opened because Apple cannot check it for malicious software" (or "is damaged and can't be opened") message. Two ways past it, once:

  • Right-click (or Control-click) Upsight.app in Applications and choose Open. Confirm in the dialog that appears. This is the standard macOS path for unsigned software and only needs doing once per machine.
  • Or, from a terminal: 
    xattr -cr /Applications/Upsight.app
    This clears the quarantine attribute Gatekeeper checks. Use it if the right-click path does not offer an Open option.

docs.title: Runtime dependencies
docs.text:
The app itself needs nothing beyond the .dmg. A handful of features shell out to external CLIs and need those on PATH separately. Install only what you use, the app runs fine without the rest, and a feature missing its CLI just no-ops (upsight doctor, see below, tells you exactly what is missing).

Feature Dependency Install Win-wire PDF text extraction pdftotext (poppler) brew install poppler AI features (meeting summaries, CX indicators, agenda enhancement, "Investigate" on a failed write-back) the claude CLI curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh \| bash, then claude login Salesforce integration (account/case sync, optional write-back) the sf CLI npm install -g @salesforce/cli, then sf org login web Tableau dashboards surfaced to AI generation (optional, only if configured in Settings) npx running @tableau/mcp-server brew install node (gives you npx), then npm install -g @tableau/mcp-server@2.21.1 to seed the cache

A few notes on those:

  • Clipboard copy and desktop notifications need nothing. macOS's built-in pbcopy/pbpaste and osascript are used automatically.
  • The Salesforce CLI is deliberately installed via npm, not Homebrew. Homebrew's salesforce-cli cask is deprecated upstream and fails the Gatekeeper check; npm is Salesforce's own documented install path (and the one sf update expects). If you don't already have Node, get it first: brew install node.
  • The AI binary is configurable. claude is the default, but any CLI that reads a prompt on stdin and writes to stdout works. See Settings and the [ai] section of config.toml (binary / args) to point at a different one (for example the Gemini CLI).
  • Tableau MCP is seeded, not just installed. The app invokes it as npx -y --prefer-offline @tableau/mcp-server@2.21.1 at AI-generation time. --prefer-offline means it resolves from npm's local cache rather than hitting the network on every AI call, so the one-time global install above is what makes that fast and avoids a network round-trip, rather than strictly required. npx would still fetch it fresh each time without it.
  • After installing what you need, run upsight doctor from a terminal (or the Doctor panel in Settings) to confirm everything the app can see is wired up correctly, including an optional --ai check that runs one real generation through your configured AI binary.

docs.title: What the app expects at runtime
Database and config locations
docs.text:
Upsight stores its data in a single SQLite file. The database path is the same on every platform:

~/.local/share/upsight/upsight.db

config.toml, however, follows the macOS convention rather than Linux's:

~/Library/Application Support/upsight/config.toml

Set the UPSIGHT_DB environment variable before launching to point the app at a different database file, useful if you keep it on a synced volume:

export UPSIGHT_DB="$HOME/sync/upsight/upsight.db"

Upsight is a local, single-user app. To use it on more than one machine, keep the database file in a directory that Syncthing replicates (brew install syncthing if you want it, or grab the cask). The app opens the database in WAL mode with a single writer, so only run one instance at a time against a given file; Syncthing also replicates the -wal and -shm sidecar files, so let a sync settle before opening the app on another machine. See Multi-machine sync.

docs.title: Credential storage
docs.text: Integration credentials (Salesforce, Aha, Clari, Todoist, and similar) are stored in the macOS Keychain, not in config.toml. The first time you save one in Settings, macOS may prompt you to allow Upsight to access the keychain. Approve it, or the app can't read the credential back on the next launch.

docs.title: Salesforce write-back
docs.text: Editing posture and other fields always saves locally and queues the change. Pushing those changes back to Salesforce is off by default, because it writes to your live org. Turn it on in Settings under Integrations, Salesforce, "Push field edits back to Salesforce", then relaunch the app. With it off, your edits are kept and queued but nothing is sent to Salesforce.

docs.title: Install on NixOS
docs.text:
Upsight ships a Nix flake. This page shows how to add it to a NixOS or home-manager configuration and install the desktop app.

The package is Linux only. It links the WebKitGTK 6.0 webview, which has no buildable Nix counterpart on macOS. On a Darwin system the package is marked broken and will not build.

docs.title: Add the flake input
docs.text:
Add the repository to the inputs of your system flake and point it at nixpkgs so it does not pull a second copy:

{
  inputs = {
    nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-26.05";

    upsight = {
      url = "github:bashfulrobot/upsight";
      inputs.nixpkgs.follows = "nixpkgs";
    };
  };
}

Upsight tracks nixos-26.05. Using the same nixpkgs avoids building the app and its dependencies twice.

docs.title: Install via the overlay
docs.text:
The flake exposes overlays.default, which adds upsight to your package set. Apply the overlay, then reference pkgs.upsight anywhere you list packages.

In a NixOS configuration:

{ inputs, pkgs, ... }:
{
  nixpkgs.overlays = [ inputs.upsight.overlays.default ];

  environment.systemPackages = [ pkgs.upsight ];
}

docs.title: Install via the package directly
docs.text:
If you do not want the overlay, reference the package output for your system:

{ inputs, pkgs, ... }:
{
  environment.systemPackages = [
    inputs.upsight.packages.${pkgs.system}.upsight
  ];
}

inputs.upsight.packages.${pkgs.system}.default is the same derivation, so either attribute works.

docs.title: Install with home-manager
docs.text:
The same two options apply in a home-manager module. With the overlay:

{ inputs, pkgs, ... }:
{
  nixpkgs.overlays = [ inputs.upsight.overlays.default ];

  home.packages = [ pkgs.upsight ];
}

Or reference the package directly:

{ inputs, pkgs, ... }:
{
  home.packages = [
    inputs.upsight.packages.${pkgs.system}.upsight
  ];
}

docs.title: Minimal flake example
docs.text:
A complete flake.nix for a single NixOS host that installs Upsight:

{
  inputs = {
    nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-26.05";

    upsight = {
      url = "github:bashfulrobot/upsight";
      inputs.nixpkgs.follows = "nixpkgs";
    };
  };

  outputs = { self, nixpkgs, upsight, ... }:
    {
      nixosConfigurations.myhost = nixpkgs.lib.nixosSystem {
        system = "x86_64-linux";
        modules = [
          ({ pkgs, ... }: {
            nixpkgs.overlays = [ upsight.overlays.default ];
            environment.systemPackages = [ pkgs.upsight ];

            # ... the rest of your host configuration ...
          })
        ];
      };
    };
}

Build and switch the host with your usual command (for example nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#myhost). After the rebuild, upsight is on PATH and the app appears in your desktop launcher.

docs.title: What the app expects at runtime
Database location
docs.text:
Upsight stores its data in a single SQLite file. The default path is:

~/.local/share/upsight/upsight.db

Set the UPSIGHT_DB environment variable to point at a different file:

export UPSIGHT_DB="$HOME/sync/upsight/upsight.db"

Upsight is a local, single-user app. To use it on more than one machine, keep the database file in a directory that Syncthing replicates. The app opens the database in WAL mode with a single writer, so only run one instance at a time against a given file. Syncthing also replicates the -wal and -shm sidecar files; let a sync settle before opening the app on another machine.

docs.title: Credential storage
docs.text: Integration credentials (Salesforce, Aha, Clari, Todoist, and similar) are stored in the operating system keyring through libsecret. On Linux this is the Secret Service backend, which a keyring daemon such as GNOME Keyring or KWallet provides. Make sure a Secret Service provider is running in your session; otherwise credential reads and writes fail and integrations stay disabled. On macOS the same code path uses the system Keychain.

docs.title: Salesforce write-back
docs.text: Editing posture and other fields always saves locally and queues the change. Pushing those changes back to Salesforce is off by default, because it writes to your live org. Turn it on in Settings under Integrations, Salesforce, "Push field edits back to Salesforce", then relaunch the app. With it off, your edits are kept and queued but nothing is sent to Salesforce.

docs.title: Wayland (Hyprland and other wlroots compositors)
docs.text: On Linux the app disables WebKit's accelerated DMA-BUF and compositing render paths (WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER and WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE), which otherwise crash the webview when the window is unmapped by a workspace switch. Both are set only when unset, so you can override them if your setup needs different rendering behaviour.

docs.title: Meeting summaries
docs.text: The Meetings tab inside an account lists past and upcoming meetings. For past meetings, Upsight can generate an AI summary from the transcript or notes.

docs.title: How summaries work
docs.text:
The app passes meeting content to the claude CLI and receives a structured summary with key topics, decisions, and action items. The CLI must be on your PATH and authenticated for this to work.

A generated summary appears in the meeting detail panel on the right side of the Meetings screen. If none has been generated yet, the panel shows the raw notes.

Copy a summary in two formats, full Markdown or Slack Markdown, using the format buttons in the meeting detail.

docs.title: The upsight summarize CLI
docs.text:
Upsight ships a companion CLI subcommand for batch-generating meeting summaries from transcripts stored on your filesystem.

upsight summarize

The CLI looks for transcript files in a configured folder structure and matches each folder to an Upsight account by name. It then generates and stores the summary inside Upsight.

docs.title: Folder-to-account mapping
docs.text:
The CLI matches folder names to account names automatically when the names are the same (or close enough after normalization). When a folder name is an abbreviation or would match more than one account, you must add an explicit mapping.

Add mappings in Settings under General, "Meeting summaries." Each row maps a folder name (as the CLI sees it on disk) to a specific Upsight account. Folders that already match by name need no entry here.

The folder name match is case-insensitive.

docs.title: Editing a summary
docs.text: If a generated summary is wrong or incomplete, you can edit it directly. Open the meeting in the Meetings tab, scroll to the summary, and click the edit icon. Your edits save locally and replace the generated content.

docs.title: Marking meetings as processed
docs.text: Once you review a meeting and act on its action items, you can mark it as processed using the toggle in the meeting detail panel. Processed meetings stay in the list but look different from pending ones.

docs.title: Logging activity
docs.text: From the meeting detail you can log a CX activity tied to the meeting. This creates an activity record linked to the meeting date and the relevant contact.

docs.title: Monthly CX update
docs.text: The Monthly CX Update is a guided wizard that walks you through refreshing an account's health picture for the month: ten health indicators, an overall sentiment score, a handful of renewal-related fields, and an executive summary entry. It is not a document you draft and copy, it is the flow that actually updates the account's posture in Salesforce.

docs.title: How the due date works
docs.text: Upsight tracks which accounts have a completed update for the current month and surfaces a reminder banner (top of the Dashboard, "Monthly CX Updates, N remaining") starting from a configured day of the month. Set the due day in Settings under General, "Monthly CX Update" (see Settings). The app does not enforce a strict deadline. It just keeps the banner, and each account's count toward it, visible until that account's update is submitted.

docs.title: Starting the wizard
docs.text: Click Start on the Dashboard banner to walk every remaining account in turn. To update a single account instead, open it and use its Overview tab quick actions to launch the wizard scoped to just that account.

docs.title: Working through an account
docs.text:
For each account the wizard shows:

  • Ten health indicators (Consumption, Enterprise Features, Kong OSS Present, Critical Use Cases, Customer Business Health, Relationship Health, Technical Engagement, Platform Play, Value Realization, Active Project), each a Red/Yellow/Green status plus a free-text comment.
  • Account Health Score, a sentiment status and comment, tracked separately from the ten indicators.
  • CX Play, Notes for Support, Expected Production Date, Renewal Risk Level, Customer Stage, and ARR Churn Forecast. Renewal Risk Level and ARR Churn Forecast route to the account's next open renewal opportunity and only appear when one exists.
  • Executive summary, a free-text entry that gets prepended (with your name and the date) to the account's running exec-summary notes rather than replacing them.

Every field shows the account's current value alongside the one you are editing, so you can see exactly what would change.

docs.title: Using AI suggestions
docs.text: Each indicator, the sentiment score, and the executive summary have their own Generate button that asks your configured AI binary for a suggested status and comment from the account's current data. A field generates independently of the others, so one slow or failed generation does not hold up the rest. Review every suggestion before accepting it. Nothing saves until you accept a field or type over it yourself.

docs.title: Saving and moving to the next account
docs.text:
• Submit & next writes every changed field back to Salesforce, marks this account's update complete for the month (clearing it from the reminder count), and advances to the next account.
  • Skip account advances without saving anything for this account.
  • Save & close saves whatever you have entered so far without marking the month complete and without advancing, so you can pick the account back up later from where you left off.

A running count of changes sits in the footer; click it to review, and revert, any single pending edit before you submit.

When you reach the last account, the wizard shows how many accounts were saved, skipped, or could not be saved (a genuine Salesforce load failure, distinct from a deliberate skip) before returning you to the Dashboard.

docs.title: Editing one indicator outside the wizard
docs.text: You do not have to run the whole wizard to fix a single indicator. On an account's Health tab, click any indicator's status pill to open a small editor for just its status and notes. This has no AI suggestion and does not affect the monthly-complete tracking, it is a plain manual edit that saves locally and queues for Salesforce write-back the same way any other field edit does.

docs.title: Multi-machine sync
docs.text: Upsight is a local, single-machine app. To use it on more than one machine, put the database file in a directory that Syncthing replicates, then point each machine's app at that shared file.

docs.title: Setup overview
docs.text:
1. Install Syncthing on both machines and add them to a shared folder.
  2. Put your Upsight database in the shared folder, or move it there.
  3. Set the UPSIGHT_DB environment variable on each machine to point at the file in the shared folder.
  4. Configure .stignore on both machines to exclude transient SQLite files (see below).

docs.title: Pointing the app at the shared file
docs.text:
Set UPSIGHT_DB before launching Upsight:

export UPSIGHT_DB="$HOME/sync/upsight/upsight.db"

Put this in your shell profile or session environment so it applies on every launch. When set, the app always uses that path instead of the default.

docs.title: One instance at a time
docs.text:
Run only one instance of Upsight against a given database file at a time. The app opens the database in WAL mode with a single writer, so running two instances against the same file at once corrupts it.

On a two-machine setup, close the app on machine A, wait for Syncthing to finish syncing (the tray icon shows progress), then open it on machine B.

docs.title: Syncthing .stignore patterns
docs.text:
SQLite writes several transient sidecar files Syncthing should not sync. Add these patterns to the .stignore file for your Upsight sync folder:

upsight.db-wal
upsight.db-shm
upsight.db.lock
*.db.backup-v*
*.pre-restore
config.toml.tmp
config.toml.bak
upsight.session.tmp
*.sync-conflict-*

The same list is shown in Settings under Data, Sync.

upsight.db-wal and upsight.db-shm are the WAL journal files SQLite writes while the database is open. Syncing them to another machine while the app is running would corrupt the database there. upsight.db.lock stops Syncthing from replicating an open lock file. *.db.backup-v* and *.pre-restore exclude Upsight's own backup and pre-restore copies so they do not bloat the sync folder. config.toml.tmp and config.toml.bak are transient config writes. upsight.session.tmp is a temporary session file.

*.sync-conflict-* suppresses Syncthing's own conflict copies. If a conflict file appears (which should not happen if you follow the one-instance rule), do not open it in Upsight. Instead, inspect both copies and decide which one to keep, then delete the other.

docs.title: Letting a sync settle
docs.text:
After closing the app on one machine, wait for Syncthing to finish syncing before opening it on another. Syncthing replicates the -wal and -shm sidecar files alongside the main database file. Opening the app mid-sync risks reading a half-transferred checkpoint.

A short wait, 10 to 30 seconds after the Syncthing indicator goes idle, is usually enough.

docs.title: Q&A
docs.text: The Q&A tab inside an account lets you ask a free-form question and get an AI-generated answer grounded in that account's data.

docs.title: Asking a question
docs.text:
Type your question into the box at the top of the Q&A tab and click Ask. A confirmation dialog warns that the answer can take 30 seconds to several minutes to generate, since the AI reads the account's full context first. You can navigate away while it runs and the answer will be there when you come back.

The empty state shows how many channels and interactions exist for the account, as a rough sense of how much grounding is available before you ask.

docs.title: What the answer is grounded in
docs.text:
Each question is answered fresh. Upsight builds a context block from the account's profile, win-wire history, account-state summary, recent meeting summaries, active cases, opportunities, contacts, consumption posture, ranked Aha ideas, and REACH scores, then sends that block plus your question to the AI in one prompt. There is no conversation memory. Every question is answered from scratch, not as a follow-up to the previous one.

Answers cite their sources inline, as backticked filenames or REACH values, so you can trace a claim back to where it came from.

docs.title: Question history
docs.text: The list on the Q&A tab shows your questions and answers for the current app session, most recent first, capped at the last 10. This history is not saved between sessions and clears when you switch accounts. To keep an answer permanently, save it as a document (below).

docs.title: Saving an answer
docs.text: Click "Save as document" under any answered question to store it as a Markdown file in the account's Documents tab. The file is named with a timestamp and includes the question and the full answer.

docs.title: Salesforce integration
docs.text: Upsight reads from and writes to Salesforce through your locally installed sf CLI. The app never handles your Salesforce credentials directly.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Log in once with the Salesforce CLI:

sf org login web

This opens a browser, authenticates against Kong's production Salesforce org, and stores the session in the CLI's own credential store. Upsight picks it up on the next sync.

To check whether the app sees an authenticated session, go to Settings, then Integrations, then Salesforce. The status indicator shows your authenticated username or "Not authenticated."

You can also start the login flow from Settings, which shows the command and the auth-status indicator.

docs.title: Syncing data from Salesforce
docs.text:
Upsight pulls Salesforce data on demand. Open an account and click the sync button in the account header (the rotating-arrows icon above the tab strip) to pull the latest data.

Reads are read-only SELECT queries against the live Kong production org.

docs.title: Salesforce write-back (off by default)
docs.text:
Write-back is the path that pushes your local edits (posture fields, health indicators, notes) back to Salesforce. It is off by default, because turning it on writes to the live Kong org.

With write-back off:

  • Edits still save locally and appear in the UI immediately.
  • Changes queue in the local database.
  • Nothing leaves your machine.

To enable write-back: go to Settings, Integrations, Salesforce, and turn on "Push field edits back to Salesforce", then relaunch the app.

Once enabled, a field edit pushes after a short debounce. A background drain retries any failures automatically.

Before enabling, check the Sync Log to review any queued edits from earlier sessions. Open it by clicking "Sync Log" at the bottom of the left sidebar. Those queued edits push on the first launch after you enable write-back.

docs.title: The sf CLI path
docs.text: By default the app finds the sf CLI on your PATH. If you need to point it at a specific binary, set a custom path under Settings, Integrations, Salesforce. Toggle "Auto" off and enter the absolute path to the binary.

docs.title: Cases
docs.text: Cases are pulled from Salesforce and displayed read-only. There is no case write-back; case management stays in Salesforce.

docs.title: Jira and Slack links
docs.text: If a case has a linked Jira ticket or Slack thread in Salesforce, a matching button appears on the case and opens that URL in your default browser. Hover over the button first to see which host it points to.

docs.title: Escalation and staleness indicators
docs.text:
Two indicators surface on the Cases list and case detail pane, both computed locally from data already synced (nothing new to configure):

  • Escalated (red activity icon): the case's Status is one of "Escalated to Eng," "Escalated to Services," or "Internal Escalation," or the case has a Jira ticket linked. Closed and solved cases never show this, even if they were escalated at some point, since the escalation is no longer active.
  • Stale (amber clock icon): the case is open and its most recent comment (or its creation date, if it has never had a comment) is more than a week old. Closed and solved cases never show this either.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Settings is reachable from the bottom of the left sidebar. It is organized into six sections: General, Integrations, AI, Catalogs, Data, and About.

docs.title: General
docs.text:
Appearance. Choose Light, Dark, or System for the color theme. System follows your OS setting. Density switches between Comfortable and Compact; Compact tightens row heights to show more data per screen.

Monthly CX Update. Set the day of month when the CX update reminder becomes visible for accounts without a completed update. Accepts 1 through 28.

Meeting summaries. Map folder names to Upsight accounts for the upsight summarize CLI. Add a row when a folder name does not match an account automatically (for abbreviations or ambiguous names). Folders that already match by name need no mapping here.

Clipboard. Upsight detects available clipboard tools (wl-copy, xclip, xsel) and uses the first one it finds. To use a specific tool, select it from the dropdown. The detected or configured tool is shown next to the label.

Notifications. Enable desktop notifications for Salesforce sync results and new Slack touchpoints.

Keyboard shortcuts. A reference list of all keyboard shortcuts in the app.

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text:
Salesforce. Shows the authentication status of your sf CLI session. Click "Log in to Salesforce" if not authenticated. You can also set a custom path to the sf binary if it is not on your PATH.

Todoist. Enter your Todoist API token to enable task sync. Find the token in Todoist under Settings, Integrations, Developer. After saving, use "Test" to verify the connection. Revoke and regenerate this token from Todoist Settings if you suspect it was exposed.

Aha! Enter your Aha! API credentials to enable feature request sync. A "Test" button verifies the connection. The separate "Post comments to Aha!" toggle gates whether Upsight can post a comment back to an Aha! idea.

Clari Copilot. Enter your Clari Copilot API credentials to pull conversation intelligence data. Find credentials in Clari under Workspace Settings, Integrations, Clari Copilot API.

Google Calendar. Paste your Google Calendar private ICS URL to pull upcoming meeting events. Find the URL in Google Calendar under Settings, "Settings for my calendars," select your calendar, "Integrate calendar," then "Secret address in iCal format." Use "Test" to verify the sync. This URL is a permanent bearer credential. Treat it like a password and do not share it.

Slack. Enter your Slack channel name and Client ID for Slack integration. The Slack channel is used for product updates and release touchpoints.

Product updates retention. Sets how many days of Slack-sourced product update records to keep (default 90).

Salesforce write-back. "Push field edits back to Salesforce" enables the drain that sends locally queued field changes to Salesforce. This is off by default. See Salesforce integration for the full details.

Todoist ship events. Gates whether Upsight offers a "create Todoist task" button when an Aha idea reaches a shipped status in the Events feed.

Todoist suggested tasks. Enables periodic suggestions for stale Todoist tasks linked to your accounts. Set the check interval and how many inactive days trigger a suggestion.

docs.title: AI
docs.text:
The AI section configures the claude CLI used for generating meeting summaries and other AI features. By default Upsight finds claude on your PATH. Toggle "Auto" off to set a custom path to the binary.

The AI section also shows the resolved binary path after detection.

docs.title: Catalogs
docs.text:
Catalogs define the master lists for the Stack screen: Products and Infrastructure. You can add, edit, and archive catalog entries here. Each entry has a name, category, and an active flag (inactive entries are hidden from the Stack pickers but not deleted).

The undo button restores the last deleted catalog entry.

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
Database. Shows the current database path, file size, schema version, integrity status, and last backup timestamp. "Compact (VACUUM)" rewrites the database to recover space. "Back up now" takes an immediate snapshot.

Automatic backups. Set how often backups run (in hours) and how many daily and weekly snapshots to keep. Changes take effect on the next launch.

Data Maintenance. "Backfill Win Wires from Salesforce" re-syncs every win wire record against Salesforce to pull the authoritative close date, ACV, TCV, opportunity name, owner, and stage. Safe to run anytime.

Import / Export. Export selected accounts to a bundle ZIP or import a bundle from another Upsight instance. See Backup and restore for details.

Sync. Shows the .stignore patterns to add to your Syncthing folder config. See Multi-machine sync for details.

docs.title: About
docs.text:
Paths. Shows the locations of the config file, database, and session file.

Diagnostics. Shows the logs directory and the backup directory, with buttons to open the log folder and take an immediate backup.

Privacy. Toggle the crash-report dialog. When enabled, an uncaught exception shows a redacted report you can copy and file as a GitHub issue. Nothing is sent automatically.

Version. Shows the app version and build stack.

docs.title: Win wires
docs.text: The Win Wires tab, inside an account, holds closed-won write-ups: what was sold, the deal terms, and the competitive context. Upsight can generate one from a PDF, or you can enter one by hand.

docs.title: Generating a win wire from a PDF
docs.text:
Click Add, then Extract from PDF in the dialog that opens. This opens a native file picker to choose the PDF. Upsight extracts the PDF's text and sends it to your configured AI CLI, which returns a structured draft: the opportunity name, close date, ACV, TCV, term length, category, sales play, competitors, champion, owner, and required capabilities.

This needs both pdftotext (poppler) and the AI CLI (claude by default) on PATH. See Install on macOS for how to install them, or upsight doctor to check what is missing.

The extracted draft is saved as soon as extraction finishes, review and edit any field, then click Add to keep it. Closing the dialog without saving discards the draft entirely, nothing is left behind.

docs.title: Entering one manually
docs.text: Open the same Add dialog and fill in the fields yourself, skipping Extract from PDF. Every field the AI extraction fills in is also a plain editable field.

docs.title: Reviewing and editing
docs.text: Click a win wire in the list to expand it. Use Open the source PDF to view the original file (only available for entries created from a PDF), or the edit button to change any field. Editing works the same whether the entry came from AI extraction or manual entry.

docs.title: Keeping win wires in sync with Salesforce
docs.text: Salesforce can also supply win wire entries directly, and a win wire linked to a Salesforce Opportunity can be refreshed from there. In Settings, under Data Maintenance, Backfill Win Wires from Salesforce re-syncs every win wire against its linked Opportunity: it pulls the authoritative close date, ACV/TCV, opportunity name, owner, and stage, then renames the PDF to a canonical filename. This is safe to run any time, already-enriched rows are just refreshed, and the button reports how many were enriched, renamed, skipped, or failed.
